title: Making Things Happen in Your Career
text: Identify a realistic career-related goal and describe clear, practical actions you can take to make progress towards it.
cdi_links: 4.C.02 Starting to take responsibility for making things happen in their career

title: Introduction
bullets: Take responsibility for your future choices as you prepare to leave school
Understand how small, realistic actions can move you towards your goals
Set a career-related goal and break it into achievable steps
Identify possible barriers and create a simple action plan to support your progress

title: Success Criteria
bullets: I can identify a personal or career-related goal
I can explain why this goal is important to me
I can break my goal into small, achievable steps
I can take responsibility for my progress by choosing realistic actions
I can begin developing an action plan with next steps and possible deadlines

title: Key Words
bullets: Action Plan – A clear list of steps that move you from where you are now towards a goal
Accountability – Accepting responsibility for your choices, actions, and progress
Milestones – Small achievements or checkpoints that show you’re moving in the right direction
Barriers – Things that might get in the way of progress and strategies to overcome them

title: Starter Activity
bullets: Why do you think some people struggle to make progress towards their goals?
Do you prefer working towards big goals or small goals? Why?

title: Taking Responsibility
bullets: Taking responsibility means recognising that your actions shape your future
Employers value people who show initiative
It helps you feel more confident and in control
Small steps lead to big changes over time

title: Breaking a Goal Down
bullets: Large goals can feel overwhelming, so break them into smaller steps
Example: Goal – Get a part-time job
Steps: Update or create a CV, ask for feedback, look for vacancies, visit shops to enquire, apply for at least two roles each week

title: Action Plan
bullets: An action plan records your goal, the steps needed, resources/support, possible deadlines, and how you will hold yourself accountable
It helps you stay focused and on track without being complicated

title: Activity – Plan Your Goal
text: Set one personal or career-related goal. List three actions you can take to move towards it, then create a simple action plan including: possible completion date, someone who can support you, and how you will stay on track.

title: Key Takeaways
bullets: Taking responsibility and breaking goals into achievable steps increases confidence and progress
Action plans and accountability help overcome barriers and keep you on track
